prompt.context: Our client is a mid-size school district with 150 schools, serving grades 1st through 12th. The district has had poor performance over the past five years and recently hired a new Chancellor to improve performance. In turn, the Chancellor hired McKinsey to identify ways to improve the district.
prompt.question: What are some of the key drivers that may be affecting performance?

clarifying_info.q: What type of performance needs to be improved — student performance or budgetary performance?
Are the functions in the exhibit related to central headquarters?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, functions are related to central headquarters.

clarifying_info.q: What do the average number of requests represent?
clarifying_info.a: These are requests or complaints made by individual school principals to HQ.

clarifying_info.q: What does days of effort mean?
clarifying_info.a: Days of effort is the amount of time required for HQ to respond to the principal's request or complaint.

clarifying_info.q: For the math curriculum improvement, can we assume similar 10% gains in subsequent years?

exhibits.title: Back-Office Support Functions: Principal Survey and Request Data
exhibits.shows: A table of six back-office functions at central HQ, showing the percentage of principals who identified each function as a key factor affecting performance, the average number of requests per principal per month, and the average days of effort for the function to answer per request.

framework: Internal factors (within the district's control): facilities, back-office support (IT/Finance/HR), curriculum, enrichment programs, teacher quality, management quality

External factors (beyond the district's control): proportion of well-educated parents vs. national/state average, student engagement, poor student preparation prior to 1st grade, social environment (crime rate, drug use, alcohol abuse)

questions.prompt: Look at Exhibit 1. What insights does the back-office support data provide, and which function(s) should be prioritized?
questions.guidance: Principals identify HR (60%), Facilities (50%), and IT (44%) as the top functions affecting performance. HR and Facilities are also the most utilized (2 requests/principal/month each) and take the longest to respond (5 days and 4 days respectively). A strong answer prioritizes HR and Facilities based on the combination of perceived importance and high volume/slow response time.

questions.prompt: The Chancellor estimates that additional training will reduce HR response time by 20% on average, but principals will add an additional 10% more requests as a result. How many days of effort will be saved per month across the district?
questions.guidance: Use a Before/After table. Total days = (# principals) x (requests/principal/month) x (days/request). Compare before and after, then subtract to find savings.

math.setup: Total monthly HR effort = Number of principals x requests per principal per month x days per request
steps: Before: 150 principals x 2 requests/month x 5 days/request = 1,500 days/month
After: requests increase by 10% → 2 x 1.1 = 2.2 requests/month; days decrease by 20% → 5 x 0.8 = 4 days/request
math.answer: 180 days of HR effort saved per month

questions.prompt: The district currently scores 65% on 8th grade math; the national average (target) is 85%. A new curriculum improved performance by 10% this year. If this 10% improvement is sustained and replicable each year, how long will it take the district to reach the national average?
questions.guidance: Apply compound 10% growth year over year starting from 65%. Stop when the result reaches or exceeds 85%.

math.setup: Each year the score increases by 10% of the current score (multiplicative growth). Start at 65%.
math.answer: Slightly less than 3 years to reach the 85% national average

brainstorming.prompt: What are the key drivers that may be affecting the district's student performance?

categories.name: External — Family & Community
ideas: Proportion of well-educated parents vs. national/state average
Quality of early childhood preparation before 1st grade

categories.name: External — Social Environment
ideas: Socioeconomic conditions of families in the district

recommendation: Focus on improving HR and Facilities back-office support, which are both highly cited by principals and have the highest response burden — HR training alone saves 180 days of effort per month
Roll out the successful 8th grade math curriculum across the district, with the expectation of reaching the 85% national average in approximately 3 years
risks: 10% annual improvement may not be sustainable or replicable at scale across all 150 schools
Increased HR requests (10% uptick) after training may indicate deeper HR capacity issues beyond response time
External factors (socioeconomic conditions, parental education levels) remain outside the district's control and may cap achievable gains
next_steps: Interview the 8th grade teacher who implemented the new math curriculum to understand challenges, materials, and success factors
Acquire necessary licenses and rights to the new curriculum
Communicate the curriculum change to all stakeholders — parents, teachers, principals, and students
Pilot the new curriculum in a subset of schools before district-wide rollout to validate replicability
Develop a plan to improve Facilities support in parallel with HR training
